posts.content_md:
I have a series of 9 very large holograms (approx. 11 X 11 inches each) that I would like to clean and photograph so that I can get some additional information on them. They are motion holograms in that each has about 5-8 frames where the subjects move as you change your viewing angle side to side. I suspect that they were arranged in a circular viewing frame and either you moved around the setup or the holder rotated past the viewer. They are very bright and can be viewed with a plain white light at about 30 degrees below and behind the film. I think there was a central light source in the circular viewing frame.

The subjects are shots of children from various cultures around the word. A few have hats or badges that say Union Texas, so I assume it was for a tradeshow booth or some very well to do oil executive that had these in their lobby etc.

If you have any idea about these I'd like to know. I want to photograph them and post here for the benefit of learning more about them and maybe you would enjoy seeing them too.

Regards,

Ken

Are you looking for tips on photographing holograms?

Some tips are here:

[http://www.holographyforum.org/phpBB2/v ... php?t=3623](http://www.holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewtopic.php?t=3623)

If you've got a digital camera and tripod take lots of pictures with various camera settings until you find the combination that gives you the best results for your situation. That's the really nice thing about a digital camera. If the image isn't any good it doesn't cost you anything but a little bit of time to throw it away and try again.

posts.author: BobH
posts.post_subject: Photographing & IDing Large Holograms (12 X 11 inch) - H
posts.content_md: Make the room as dark as you can, turn off the flash, and use a dark backdrop so that the light spilling off the edges of the hologram doesn't fool the light meter in the camera. Also, hold a black card (with a hole for the lens) in front of the camera for the shot. This will prevent the reflection of the camera off the hologram surface. You might also need to put some dark cloth on the tripod legs for the same reason.

posts.topic_title: Photographing & IDing Large Holograms (12 X 11 inch) - H
posts.author: Kaveh
posts.post_subject: Photographing & IDing Large Holograms (12 X 11 inch) - H
posts.content_md:
As with Colin, I have not seen these before either. I am guessing they might be Russian or East European origin.

To photograph these, if you want the greatest detail, I would recommend the following:

- Make sure you have a really good point source of light, so the image is as sharp as possible. As you have a camera and tripod, you can use a long exposure, and the image does not have to be bright. So move your reconstruction light as far away as convenient from the hologram. The image will get dimmer but sharper. I am assuming the hologram is designed to be viewed with a collimated or near-collimated beam.

- Now move your camera towards or away from the hologram till the image is a single color. Now you are in the projected 'slit' of the rainbow hologram.

- Move the camera up and down till the center of the image is the color you want the image to be.

- Move camera towards or away till the entire image is in that color. 

-Switch off flash; put camera ASA setting to minimum, e.g. 50

- Focus the image. Simple digital cameras don't normally allow manual focusing these days, but try different things till the image looks as sharp as possible. 

- If you have any control, keep the aperture as wide as possible, i.e. f/2 is better than f/16. This will minimize speckle.

- To minimize shake you could put on timer and the camera will shoot a few seconds after you press the button. 

All would be so much simpler with an old fashioned manual camera, or else a pro digital camera with full control. Good luck.

posts.content_md:
I'm baffled as to the origin of these images. It seems like they are stereograms, since it sounds like there is some animation to them. But then again, the lighting is simple, like most pulse stuff, but it's hard to tell if there is that waxy, corpse-like appearance artifact of the pulsed ruby portrait.

My guess however leans toward Advanced Dimensional Display, Craig Newswanger's company before the evil CFC took over. But then again, he probably would have transferred them so they were achromatic instead of rainbow...
